questions.scenario: You are buying a packet of chips (like Lays or Kurkure) at the local Kirana store.

options.text: I notice the quality of the plastic wrapper and how easy it is to tear open.
I read the back to see the ingredients and the funny marketing text they wrote.
I admire the bold typography, the bright colors, and the mouth-watering photo on the front.
I compare it with Doritos and think about which brand is capturing the market better.

questions.scenario: Your school is launching a new magazine and you are on the team.

options.text: I talk to the local printer shop to decide the paper quality (glossy or matte) and binding.
I decide the overall 'theme' of the magazine so it appeals to all students.
I design the actual cover page, layout, and edit the photos on Photoshop/Canva.
I assign tasks to the writers and designers and make sure it's published on time.

questions.scenario: You are buying a new t-shirt online.

options.text: I check the fabric material (cotton/polyester) and the quality of the print.
I buy it because it has a cool quote or matches my personal 'vibe'.
I choose it purely for the awesome graphic art or minimalist logo on it.
I look for a branded t-shirt so I look trendy and confident in front of friends.

questions.scenario: When you look at a massive billboard ad on the highway, what do you see?

options.text: I wonder how they printed such a giant flex banner and installed it.
I analyze who their target audience is based on the celebrity they used.
I judge the font choice, color contrast, and the layout of the poster.
I wonder how many lakhs the company paid for that prime advertising spot.

questions.scenario: You are asked to create a poster for the school Diwali Mela.

options.text: I paint it by hand on a chart paper with sketch pens and glitter.
I write a very catchy tagline that will make everyone want to buy tickets.
I use Canva/Illustrator to make a highly aesthetic digital poster with modern fonts.
I approve the final design and decide exactly which walls in the school it should be pasted on.

questions.scenario: You are unboxing a new expensive smartphone.

options.text: I love the physical feeling of peeling the plastic and sliding the smooth box open.
I read the welcome card inside and appreciate how the brand makes me feel special.
I admire the sleek logo placement and the minimalist design of the charger.
I think about how this unboxing experience justifies the high price of the phone.

questions.scenario: When buying a notebook for the new school year, which one do you pick?

options.text: The one with the thickest pages and a hard, durable cover.
The one with an inspirational quote or a smart, quirky message on the front.
The one with the most beautiful, artistic, and visually stunning cover art.
The Classmate brand, because it's reliable and a standard choice.

questions.scenario: A friend wants to start a YouTube channel and asks for your help.

options.text: I help them set up their room background, LED lights, and physical camera angles.
I brainstorm a unique name for the channel and figure out what their 'niche' should be.
I design a killer profile picture, banner, and the first thumbnail for them.
I tell them to focus on trending topics and plan a schedule to get maximum views.

questions.scenario: You are making a meme to share in your class WhatsApp group.

options.text: I just use a basic meme-generator app to quickly get the job done.
I make an inside joke that only my specific friend group will understand.
I use Photoshop to perfectly edit my friend's face onto a funny movie scene.
I make sure to post it exactly when everyone is online so it gets the most laughs.

questions.scenario: If you could redesign a famous logo (like the SBI or Parle-G logo), what would you do?

options.text: I would think about how the new logo will look printed on actual physical biscuit packets.
I wouldn't change it much, because people trust the old logo and changing it is risky.
I would completely modernize the colors, make the lines cleaner, and use a futuristic font.
I would pitch the redesign to their CEO and charge them lakhs for the rebranding.

Print_Packaging_Designer.title: Packaging & Print Designer
Print_Packaging_Designer.primary_match_text: You love the physical reality of design! You don't just want art on a screen; you want to hold it, feel the paper, and see it in the real world.
Print_Packaging_Designer.day_in_the_life: Designing product boxes, selecting paper textures, and working with printers to create physical merchandise.
Print_Packaging_Designer.alternative_match_text: Your love for physical creation also makes you a great fit for Industrial Design or Merchandise Manufacturing.
Print_Packaging_Designer.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Des in Communication Design or a Diploma in Print & Packaging.

Brand_Strategist.title: Brand Strategist / Identity Analyst
Brand_Strategist.primary_match_text: You are the brain behind the brand! You understand that design is not just about looking good, but about sending the right message and emotion.
Brand_Strategist.day_in_the_life: Researching target audiences, defining the 'personality' of a new company, and planning its visual identity.
Brand_Strategist.alternative_match_text: Because of your deep analytical thinking, you would also excel in Marketing Strategy or Copywriting.
Brand_Strategist.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th (Commerce/Arts preferred). Pursue a BBA in Marketing or BA in Advertising/PR.

Graphic_Logo_Designer.title: Graphic & Logo Designer
Graphic_Logo_Designer.primary_match_text: You are a pure visual artist! You have a natural talent for typography, colors, and transforming a blank canvas into a stunning visual.
Graphic_Logo_Designer.day_in_the_life: Creating sleek logos, designing digital posters, and crafting the core visual identity of startups on Illustrator/Photoshop.
Graphic_Logo_Designer.alternative_match_text: Your strong aesthetic sense makes you a perfect candidate for UI/UX Design or Digital Illustration.
Graphic_Logo_Designer.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th (Arts with Fine Arts is a bonus). Pursue a B.Des in Graphic Design or Visual Communication.

Art_Director.title: Art Director / Creative Head
Art_Director.primary_match_text: You are a creative leader! You have a great eye for design, but you prefer directing the overall vision and managing the big picture.
Art_Director.day_in_the_life: Leading a team of designers, approving final artworks, and pitching creative campaigns to big corporate clients.
Art_Director.alternative_match_text: With your leadership and creative management skills, you could easily build your own Design Agency or become a Marketing Head.
Art_Director.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Des or BMM, gain experience, and eventually transition to creative management.
